Build story · Oct 10–24, 2026

Roomkit

Five answers in, a whole home of real IKEA furniture out: picked by one of four engines, drawn as isometric SVGs at real size and colour, rearranged by drag, priced in your country, shared with a link, and every piece assembled step by step in 3D.

4 h 48 minagent time, Oct 10–16 (4 metered sessions)
262.8Mtokens in · 731K out
$88.47at API pricing (92% saved by caching)
Built by Forge (Claude Opus 5.5) in Empryo · deployed on Ploy · first working app in 41 min

02 · The sprite

No such sprite existed, so Forge built one

  • Web search found only flat SVG icons (GPL, no bathrooms) or tiny PNG renders
  • Took Kenney Furniture Kit: CC0 3D models incl. walls, windows, doors, floors, lamps
  • Wrote an OBJ → isometric SVG renderer: projection, flat shading, coplanar face merging, pixel-buffer depth ordering
  • Room sprite today: 276 symbols · 590 KB · 105 KB gzipped
  • Wood, fabric, walls, floor, trim are CSS variables → one sprite renders every palette
03 · The IKEA catalog

2,892 real products, each drawn to scale

  • Pulled ~8,000 products from IKEA's US search, sorted into 42 furniture types, kept the best-rated 2,892
  • Real sizes read from each product page, real colours from IKEA's colour names
  • One isometric SVG per product: nearest Kenney model, stretched to the real size, tinted the real colour
  • 18.5 MB of SVGs (2.9 MB gzipped); the browser loads only the picked ones
  • Every card links to its IKEA page with price, size and rating

04 · How it works

Five questions, live preview

  1. Brief: room (12 types) → style → palette → mood → use, budget and a note, with a live room preview that recolours and relights as you answer
  2. Engine: one of four picks 4–6 pieces from the products for that room
  3. Rules: one shared rules engine for all four: must-have pieces, one per category, hosts for TVs and stools
  4. Composer: places pieces on walls, in corners, on surfaces and on the ceiling; the sofa faces the TV; then depth-sorts the SVGs
05 · Four engines

Switch per run, keep every run

Instant

Local scoring on style, palette, budget, ratings and use. No model call, 0.0 s. The default.

Embeddings

Brief as 3 facets → weighted cosine. 0.7–5 s.

OpenAI 3 Small/Large · Gemini Embedding 2 · Qwen3 8B

Flagship LLM

Reads the category guides, returns picks, palette, title and reasons. Sonnet 5.5: 13.7 s, 9 guides read.

Opus 5.5 · Fable 5.1 · GPT-5.5 · GPT-6.1 Sol · Gemini 3.1 Pro · +5

Decisions

Choice and yes/no questions answered by decision models. 0.5 s in the benchmark.

GPT-6 Luna · Decision-1 · Jev 1.13

Regenerate with another engine and flip between runs from the result header.

06 · Result

Cards around the room they compose

Numbered markers link cards ↔ pieces · real IKEA name, price, size and rating · Day / Golden / Evening / Night lighting · one tap to the IKEA page

07 · Drag to rearrange

Move anything, nothing to lift

  • Every piece drags across the floor; things standing on it move with it
  • Wall pieces slide along their wall
  • The footprint turns red when it collides
  • Reset layout brings back the composed room
08 · Photo render

The sprite scene becomes the layout reference

Scene rasterized in the browser → sent with the prompt · Nano Banana 2.1 in 22 s here · also GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst/Flare, GPT Image 2, Gemini 3 Pro Image, Seedream 5.0 Pro, Qwen, Grok, Muse

09 · Twelve rooms

Each with its own size, windows and must-haves

Plus entryway, laundry room, studio apartment and walk-in closet. All shown here were composed by the Instant engine from real IKEA products.

10 · Whole homes

Floors, countries, accounts, a link to share

Floors and outdoors

A home is floors of rooms: ground, first, basement, attic, outside. Balcony and garden are room types with 191 outdoor IKEA pieces, grass, a tree, a fence and a railing.

Rotate anything

Hover and press R. Every product is drawn in four orientations (12,000 sprites), and whatever stands on a piece turns with it.

IKEA in 28 countries

Pick a country and every card shows the local price, currency and product link, matched by name and variant against that market's search API and cached.

Accounts and autosave

Email and password with Better Auth on Ploy SQLite. Disposable domains and "+" aliases refused, signups back off per IP, optional Turnstile.

Share with a preview

Flip "Share publicly" and get /h/sunny-flat-k3x9a2 with a generated OG image of up to three rooms drawn as sprites. An Explore page lists shared homes.

Runs on Workers

Postgres and wasm are not available on Ploy's workerd, so the database moved to Ploy SQLite and the OG image falls back to an SVG card.

11 · Assembly guides

Every piece builds itself, step by step, in 3D

  • Open a room's Assembly guide and each piece plays on a turntable: base, sides, shelves, top, back panel, doors, drawers, wall anchor
  • The small parts arrive first: dowels, cam locks, shelf pins, nails, hinges, runners, bolts, then disappear into their holes
  • Drag to turn; a finished piece spins once; the tour moves on to the next piece
  • Each step names its tool and fittings; each piece says how long it takes and whether it needs two people
  • Sizes and colours come from the product you picked, so a 6-drawer chest gets six drawers and a KALLAX its grid
12 · Matched to the listing

3,063 products, 2,632 builds, one recipe per kind of thing

  • Recipes for cabinets, wardrobes, dressers, KALLAX grids, metal racks, TROFAST boxes, tables on legs, pedestals, drawer units, sit/stand frames, shell chairs, POÄNG, sofas with chaises, beds, lofts, cribs, lamps, mirrors, carts and coat stands
  • The classifier reads the name, type, description, materials, colours and sprite model: sliding and glass doors, door and drawer counts, metal legs, padded seats
  • Drawn with the Anatomy isometric kit: four-tone shading, convex solids, draw order solved every frame from separating planes
  • npm run assembly:audit builds every product and checks it against its own listing: 28 checks, 0 overlapping parts, 0 bad geometry

14 · Guides and benchmark

The AI reads a guide before it picks

47 category guides

One markdown file per furniture type: sizes, placement rules, budget and style fit, every product. The LLM fetches only the ones it needs. Public at /guides.

Benchmark: 10 models, 24 rooms

Claude Fable 5.1 scored highest (83.8). GLM-5.3 Flash was the best value at $0.0023 a room. GPT-6 Luna Decisions answered in 0.5 s.

Placement data

Where each piece can go and how far from what: mirrors 12 cm above the vanity, coffee tables 30 cm from the sofa, the sofa about 220 cm from the TV.

The benchmark ran on Oct 12, on the first 97-product catalog, before the IKEA catalog.

18 · What broke, and the fixes

Found by testing, not by guessing

  • Reviewer fail: LLM picks skipped room rules → one shared rules function, 2,000 random checks
  • Ploy 500: Next 16.4 crashes OpenNext → reproduced in wrangler, pinned 16.3.8
  • Sofa sideways to the TV: sofa and TV sat on walls at 90° → TV first, sofa floats facing it
  • IKEA sizes mixed up: fetching product pages 12 at a time swapped dimensions → 4 at a time
  • Embeddings on the live app: [unenv] fs.readFile throws before .catch on Workers → read inside an async function
  • Gemini embeddings: max 100 texts per batch → batches capped at 100
  • Ad off the beat: a fixed tempo drifted → cuts placed on detected beats
19 · What broke in the assembly guides

Three reviewer rounds, three real bugs

1

Doors drawn behind shelves

Sorting parts by screen bounding box made false "A hides B" edges, so the order had cycles and a door could paint under the shelf behind it. Fix: a true 2D hull overlap test before an edge is added, then separating planes decide front and back.

2

Reduced motion skipped every step

With prefers-reduced-motion the guide jumped straight to the finished piece and the room tour never advanced. Fix: each finished step holds for four seconds, the tour still moves on, and the done button says Replay.

3

TOBIAS drawn as a wooden chair

Chair style came only from the materials list, and 1,288 products have none. Fix: known IKEA chair families first, then materials, then the description, colours and sprite model; and a catalog-wide audit that fails on any mismatch.

Found by an independent reviewer agent after each round, not by guessing. The audit now runs on all 3,063 products: 28 checks, 0 overlapping parts.
